notes.summary: Independently reconstructed all-cone, all-Reeb finite-target integrability criterion, genuine approximate equations, midpoint I-Cauchyness and actual-limit MA continuity. Image sufficiency remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: Using only the explicitly accepted full P13.1 mathematical theorem, the finite FS dual supremum equals the E1 dual energy and is finite exactly when every actual E1 potential is integrable. Genuine maximizing FS measures converge weakly to the target, while their potentials are I-Cauchy with bounded normalized energies. An actual E1 I-limit would realize the target, but no such limit is constructed. The fixed carrier and affine-cone probability normalization are retained.
notes.text:
These are unverified reconstructed proof claims on the unchanged original domain. Let k be any algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, (X,T;ξ) any normal good polarized affine cone, n=dim X≥1, p=n−1, and K=X0^T. The sole accepted new premise is the FULL P13.1 mathematical body embedded in the preserved input, with its explicitly accepted ORIGINAL PASS review. Its canonical notes and operational assertions are not separate mathematical premises. The round71 proof and four notes were read as unreviewed data; their results below are independently reconstructed.

Write ρ=ρξ and V=Vξ. The actual mixed probability is ν(u1,…,up)=V^(−1)ddc u1⋯ddc up ddc ρ+, and the actual energy is E(u)=(nV)^(−1)Σ(j=0,…,p)∫K u(ddc u)^j(ddc ρ)^(p−j)ddc ρ+. Here ρ|K=0, and unbounded expressions mean the accepted genuine same-field weighted decreasing limits. The accepted theorem supplies actual convexity, positive mixed probabilities, integration by parts, Hodge index, decreasing energy and weighted MA continuity, intrinsic roots, and both-sign canonical outer differentiation. It supplies no envelope attainment, actual completeness or inverse existence.

The reference probability is δ_vtriv. Rationally, its canonical product model on the normal quotient has one central component of multiplicity one and intersection equal to the volume. The accepted radial Gauss lift gives vtriv on K. Irrational references are bounded locally uniform limits of rational references, so genuine bounded current continuity gives the same Dirac measure. Normalize u(vtriv)=supK u=0. Then u≤0 and J(u)=−E(u). The rational calibration remains Vη=s^(−n)d^(1−n)(Ld^p), ωη=Ld/(sd), ωη^p=sVη, Eη=E_Ld/(sd), with effective supported gcd-one grading, actual degree-d Veronese map, one radial unit mass, and n factors 1/(sd). The signed full-ring identity remains E=(n+1)S/n.

For a Radon probability μ on K define L(μ)=sup(w∈H(ξ))[E(w)−∫w dμ]. Every test is an explicit finite primary homogeneous FS maximum. Uniform actual FS approximation and energy continuity equate this supremum with the CPSH supremum. For any decreasing bounded-above usc net h_i↓h on compact Hausdorff K, ∫h_i dμ↓∫h dμ: Radon regularity expresses the extended integral as the infimum of continuous-majorant integrals; for g≥h the increasing open sets {h_i<g+ε} cover K, so compactness and directedness give h_i≤g+ε eventually. Infimizing and letting ε↓0 proves the assertion, including −∞.

If L(μ)<∞, an actual defining CPSH net u_i↓u∈E1 satisfies ∫u_i dμ≥E(u_i)−L. Both decreasing continuities give ∫u dμ≥E(u)−L>−∞. Thus every E1 potential is integrable, and L(μ)=sup(u∈E1)[E(u)−∫u dμ]=E∨(μ). If the bounded-test supremum is infinite, the E1 supremum is already infinite.

Conversely, assume every actual E1 potential is μ-integrable. For normalized u set b_l=−∫u dν(u repeated l times,ρ repeated p−l times). These are finite and nonnegative; b_0=0 and J(u)=Σb_l/n. The actual segment u_t=tu+(1−t)ρ satisfies
J(u_t)=(1/n)Σ(l=1,…,p) t Σ(j=l,…,p) binom(j,l)t^l(1−t)^(j−l)b_l ≤2^n t²J(u).
This follows from t^(l+1)≤t² and Σ(j=l,…,p)binom(j,l)=binom(n,l+1)≤2^n, first on CPSH and then by accepted weighted decreasing limits.

Integration is uniformly bounded on normalized J≤1. Otherwise choose u_j there with ∫(−u_j)dμ≥2^j. The actual convex restrictions w_m=Σ(j≤m)2^(−j)u_j, completed off K by the remaining reference weight, decrease, have value zero at vtriv, and energy at least −1. Their actual nontrivial decreasing limit is E1, but its negative integral is infinite, a contradiction. If the bound is B, scaling with t=(2^nJ(u))^(−1/2) when J(u)≥2^(−n) gives ∫(−u)dμ≤B+B√(2^nJ(u)), hence L(μ)≤B+2^(n−2)B²<∞. Therefore L(μ)<∞ iff every actual E1 potential is integrable. This is a finite-energy TARGET criterion, without image sufficiency.

Accepted normalized roots are onto actual E1 and satisfy u/c≤Rξηu≤u/C≤0. Integrability of all source potentials therefore implies integrability of every target potential; the inverse proves the converse. The finite-energy measure class is independent of ξ on this same carrier, without transporting a strong topology.

Concavity and genuine first variation give E(w)≤E(u)+∫(w−u)dMA(u). Raw simultaneous decreasing approximation and weighted continuity extend this to E1. Thus every genuine output ν=MA(u) satisfies L(ν)=E(u)−∫u dν<∞. The opposite tangent sign printed in Wu2406.13684v1 LF1249 is not used.

Let F(g)=sup{E(w):w∈CPSH,w≤g}, and let F↓ be its continuous-majorant outer extension. For continuous g, positivity gives F(g)−∫g dμ≤L(μ). Decreasing continuous-majorant nets and the preceding integral fact extend this to every bounded-above integrable usc h. For genuine u∈E1 put d_u=L−E(u)+∫u dμ≥0. The accepted derivative in each fixed dense direction f has |F↓(u+tf)−E(u)−t∫f dMA(u)|≤C_f t², C_f=2pA(1+Aτ)^(p−1)||f||. Applying both t=s and t=−s yields |∫f d(MA(u)−μ)|≤d_u/s+C_f s. Choose u_j∈H with d_j<j^(−2). At s=1/j the error is at most (1+C_f)/j. Dense uniform approximation, with the probability error at most 2||f−f_m||, proves genuine weak convergence MA(u_j)→μ. Deficit zero gives the equation only on an already genuine potential; this is not attainment.

For p≥1, set z=u−v and B_j=−V^(−1)∫z ddc z(ddc u)^j(ddc v)^(p−1−j)ddc ρ+≥0. Hodge gives the sign, and IBP gives I(u,v)=ΣB_j. For g(t)=E(v+tz), −g''(t)=pΣ binom(p−1,j)t^j(1−t)^(p−1−j)B_j. Integrating against the midpoint Green kernel (1/2)min(t,1−t), and retaining [1/4,3/4], gives E((u+v)/2)−(E(u)+E(v))/2≥a_p I(u,v), a_p=p/4^(p+1). All coefficients are weighted mixed integrals, so raw decreasing approximation extends this to E1. Nonnegativity of the actual midpoint deficit yields I(u,v)≤(d_u+d_v)/(2a_p). Pairing with the reference gives J(u)≤I(u,0)≤(d_u+L)/(2a_p). Maximizing sequences are therefore I-Cauchy with bounded normalized energy.

For a dense direction f=a−b with actual slope-A auxiliary potentials, Hodge Cauchy–Schwarz and positive product masses A give |∫f d(MA(u)−MA(v))|≤√(2Ap||f||I(u,v)). Fixed-field decreasing approximation extends it to E1. An ACTUAL E1 I-limit of the maximizing sequence would therefore solve the equation, because its genuine MA and μ would be the same weak limit. Actual membership/completeness remains unproved.

For n=1, the accepted normal effective grading gives R=k[z], K={vtriv}, E(c)=c, and the empty horizontal product with the radial unit current gives the sole probability δ_vtriv. This case is realized uniquely modulo constants and does not cover higher dimensions.

notes.summary: A genuinely linear fixed-ray polynomial gives uniform signed target-integration error O(√deficit) on bounded-J sets and convergence of genuine output dual energies. It does not construct an inverse potential.
notes.detailedSummary: The actual fixed-ray CPSH span, its unique zero-slope extensions, a degree-(p+1) primitive and calibrated polarization satisfy exactly the finite polynomial hypotheses of Appendix A of 2307.01697v1. This justifies its Hölder estimate with α=2^(−p), without applying the full synthetic measure theorem or inventing linear axioms from roots. Combining this estimate with n1 yields uniform signed target integration, dual-energy convergence, and convergence of maximizing-sequence target integrals and normalized energies. Actual E1 membership, absolute L1 continuity on arbitrary weak potential nets, and realization remain unresolved.
notes.text:
Use n1 for actual same-field mixed products, probability normalization, target integrability, genuine approximate measures, midpoint bounds and weighted decreasing continuity. Fix one rational or irrational ξ, and p=n−1≥1. Constants C_p below depend only on p and may increase. No cross-Reeb mixed form or nonlinear root is used in this linear construction.

Let D be the real vector space spanned by restrictions of actual CPSH potentials at this ξ, including constants. It contains the accepted dense direction lattice. Every d∈D has the unique zero-slope extension d̃(v)=d(sξ(v)), followed by torification, to the punctured cone. It is a finite linear combination of genuine CPSH differences. Its distributional ddc and signed mixed products are therefore finite linear combinations of the accepted bounded products.

Take Vlin=R×D with projection onto the first coordinate. For x=(s,d), set Ω_x=s ddcρ+ddc d̃ and define the degree-(p+1) homogeneous polynomial
H(s,d)=Σ(l=0,…,p) [binom(p,l)/(l+1)]s^(p−l)V^(−1)∫d(ddc d̃)^l(ddcρ)^(p−l)ddcρ+.
Put Fpol=−H. Equivalently H=∫(t=0,…,1)V^(−1)∫d(sddcρ+tddc d̃)^pddcρ+ dt. Expanding the genuine energy and using Σ(j=l,…,p)binom(j,l)=binom(p+1,l+1) proves H(1,u)=E(u).

IBP makes all l+1 differentiated copies equal, so ∂_dH(s,d)[f]=V^(−1)∫f Ω_x^pddcρ+. Polarization gives, for zero-slope directions a,b and p−1 remaining slots,
Fpol((0,a),(0,b),x2,…,xp)=−[1/(p+1)]V^(−1)∫a ddc b̃ Ω_x2⋯Ω_xp ddcρ+.
The factor is checked by two differentiations: the derivative has coefficient −p, while degree-(p+1) polarization contributes (p+1)p. It retains the original radial normalization.

Let P consist of (s,d) with s>0 and d/s an actual CPSH restriction, together with (0,c) for constants c∈R. Actual convexity and translation make P a convex cone. The curvature of (0,c) is zero. Accepted fixed-ray Hodge gives Fpol(a,a,x2,…,xp)≥0 for every zero-slope a and positive slots xi∈P. Thus this is exactly the surjective linear projection, homogeneous polynomial, convex cone and quadratic sign setup of Appendix A of Boucksom–Jonsson2307.01697v1. This is only a FINITE POLYNOMIAL application; it does not identify an ordered global Z, ample cone, model hypotheses, generated PSH topology or actual inverse theorem.

For x=(1,u), y=(1,v), the polynomial deficit δ(x,y)=Fpol(x)−Fpol(y)−〈Fpol'(y),x−y〉 is E(v)−E(u)+∫(u−v)dMA(v). Its positive coefficient expansion gives I(u,v)/(p+1)≤δ(x,y)≤pI(u,v)/(p+1) and δ(x,y)+δ(y,x)=I(u,v). For normalized u, δ((1,u),(1,0))=J(u).

Here is the relevant proof check for the source Hölder theorem. Define q(x,y)=max(j=0,…,p−1)(x−y)^2y^jx^(p−1−j). Positive coefficients and binomial expansion make q, δ and (x−y)^2((x+y)/2)^(p−1) comparable with constants depending only on p. Put w=(x+y)/2, A=q(x,y), B=max(q(x,z),q(y,z)), and b_j=(x−y)^2z^jw^(p−1−j). Cauchy–Schwarz, 2w−x=y∈P, and convexity of δ(·,z) yield b_0≤C_pA and b_(j+1)≤b_j+C_p√(b_jB). When A≤B, induction gives b_(p−1)≤C_p A^(2^(1−p))B^(1−2^(1−p)); when A≥B, the seminorm triangle inequality gives b_(p−1)≤4B. Applying this to x−z and y−z with positive slot w gives q(x,y)≤C_p T^(2^(1−p))max(q(x,y),T)^(1−2^(1−p)), T=max(q(x,z),q(y,z)). Absorbing the q power when q>T proves the quasi-triangle inequality, without assuming it earlier.

Averaging remaining positive slots and another Cauchy–Schwarz inequality then give the mixed estimate |(x0−y0)(x1−y1)z2⋯zp|≤C_pδ(x0,y0)^αδ(x1,y1)^αM^(1−2α), α=2^(−p), where M is the maximum deficit to a fixed reference. Expanding x0^p−y0^p and applying Cauchy–Schwarz gives |〈Fpol'(x0)−Fpol'(y0),x1−y1〉|≤C_pδ(x0,y0)^(1/2)δ(x1,y1)^αM^(1/2−α). For p=1 this is ordinary quadratic Cauchy–Schwarz.

Consequently, on normalized actual continuous potentials,
|∫(u−v)d(MA(w)−MA(z))|≤C_p I(w,z)^(1/2)I(u,v)^α max{J(u),J(v),J(w),J(z)}^(1/2−α).
Raw decreasing approximation extends this to E1. Normalized approximants need not decrease: their integrals and energies differ from the raw decreasing ones only by their convergent constants at vtriv. Accepted weighted continuity passes every term. All products remain at this fixed ξ, including irrational ξ.

Now let μ have finite L=L(μ). Choose normalized genuine maximizing w_k∈H with deficits d_k→0 and d_k≤1. By n1, J(w_k)≤B0, where B0=1+(L+1)/(2a_p) and a_p=p/4^(p+1). For genuine normalized ψ and φ, use u=φ,v=0,w=ψ,z=w_k. Midpoint Cauchyness and I(φ,0)≤(p+1)J(φ) give
|∫φ d(MA(ψ)−MA(w_k))|≤C_p√(d_ψ+d_k)J(φ)^α[J(φ)+J(ψ)+B0]^(1/2−α).
For continuous φ, genuine weak convergence lets k→∞. For unbounded φ, first fix each continuous defining approximant, send k→∞, and only then send its defining net to φ. The fixed target uses n1 decreasing integrals; the fixed MA(ψ) uses accepted weighted continuity. Normalization constants tend to zero. This proves
|∫φ d(MA(ψ)−μ)|≤C_p√d_ψ J(φ)^α[J(φ)+J(ψ)+B0]^(1/2−α).
For p=1 the last factor is one. This order of limits avoids passing an unbounded moving test through weak measure convergence.

Along the maximizing sequence, uniformly over normalized J(φ)≤B, the error is at most C_p√d_j B^α(B+2B0)^(1/2−α). This is convergence of SIGNED integrals on bounded-energy sets. Putting φ=w_j and using n1 tangent optimality gives |L(MA(w_j))−L(μ)|≤d_j+C_p√d_j B0^(1/2). Thus genuine output measures converge weakly and in dual energy, without implying that their target is realized.

Also compare MA(w_j) with the reference and send j→∞ in the same order. For normalized u,v∈E1,
|∫(u−v)dμ|≤C_p I(u,v)^α B0^(1/2)[B0+J(u)+J(v)]^(1/2−α).
The target integrals of a normalized maximizing sequence are therefore Cauchy. Since E(w_j)−∫w_jdμ→L, its normalized energies also converge to a finite value. These conclusions strengthen bounded energies, but supply no actual potential limit, weak compactness or absolute L1 continuity along arbitrary nonmonotone weak potential nets.

The exact applied source is 2307.01697v1, PDF SHA256 979daddbb2082320cd6bbe6f8522535e68b56d229317decd033c3101b9fdbaa1, extract SHA256 8068829692eeb5ddcfd40de5a6141f415601c5b493e5578ad63e0dd3140bf2e4. notes.summary: Strict logarithmic supports, pole-sensitive rational AFS approximation, normal divisor-order localization and carrier-envelope retraction are reconstructed. The normal weak Runge and rational envelope base remain unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: The explicit log-sum-exp construction has strict real support contacts even at infinite coordinates. Multinomial maxima retain original generators, and nested rational coefficients with local floors approximate singular real supports decreasingly. Normality simplifies pole clearing inside the original ring. A continuous-retraction lemma identifies carrier usc regularizations without openness, and raw roots transfer carrier membership after a base exists. These results do not establish the represented metric, weak trace/Runge, finite-projection, singular-induction or arbitrary-field envelope chain.
notes.text:
Use n1 for the accepted rational quotient, residual torification, actual raw roots and carrier conventions. The elementary constructions below independently reconstruct portions of the unreviewed root79 proposal. The round70 body and notes were documentary data, not supporting theorems. No corrected singular EP theorem is assumed.

For N≥1 choose integer a≥log(N+1) and set χ_N(t)=a^(−1)log(1+Σexp(−at_i)) on (R∪{+∞})^N, with exp(−a∞)=0. It is continuous, coordinatewise decreasing and convex on finite coordinates, and lies between max(0,−t_i) and that maximum plus one. At t let I be the finite coordinates and p_i=exp(−at_i)/(1+Σ(i∈I)exp(−at_i)). The support ℓ_t(s)=χ_N(t)−Σ(i∈I)p_i(s_i−t_i) has zero coefficient on every infinite coordinate; a supported coordinate becoming infinite gives value −∞. Log-sum convexity gives χ_N≥ℓ_t with equality exactly at t. On the finite face, the extra positive constant term gives strict convexity. Making a formerly infinite coordinate finite strictly increases χ_N.

For every neighborhood U of t, χ_N−ℓ_t has a positive gap outside U. In a nonzero finite-coordinate recession direction v, max(0,−v_i)+Σp_iv_i>0 because every p_i>0 and Σp_i<1. Thus a bounded-difference sublevel confines supported finite coordinates. It also bounds every remaining coordinate below; a coordinate tending to −∞ sends χ_N to +∞. The closure is compact in the extended product, and a supported coordinate tending to +∞ sends the difference to +∞. The remaining compact sublevel has singleton zero set {t}, proving the gap, including I empty.

An actual rational AFS approximation follows from the multinomial identity. Set z0=1, z_i=exp(−at_i), B_m=binom(m+N,N), and
q_m(t)=max(|β|=m)[−Σ(i≥1)(β_i/m)t_i+log binom(m;β)/(am)].
The maximum summand is between (Σz_i)^m/B_m and (Σz_i)^m, so q_m≤χ_N≤q_m+log B_m/(am), uniformly on the entire extended product. Terms having β_i>0 at t_i=∞ are −∞, while β0=m supplies a zero floor. Choose m_j so this error is ≤ε_j/4 and round intercepts upward rationally with error ≤ε_j/4. Adding ε_j with rational ε_(j+1)≤ε_j/4 gives a decreasing sequence: its lower excess at level j exceeds its upper excess at level j+1. It converges to χ_N.

After t_i=−log|f_i|, each branch is m^(−1)log|Πf_i^β_i| plus a rational intercept. When the list includes the original affine algebra generators, the terms β_i=1,β0=m−1 contain the generators themselves. These are actual finite AFS presentations with generator branches and floor, not merely presentations by generator powers.

Real singular support coefficients require a pole-sensitive approximation. Let H≥0 be a rational AFS exhaustion in the original generators, enlarged so log|f_i|≤D_iH with integers D_i≥1. For strictly positive real p_i, choose nested rational q_ij↑p_i and r_ij↓p_i. Put F_ij=max(log|f_i|,2^(−j)H−j), ε_j=ΣD_i(r_ij−q_ij), and rational C_j↓C. Then
L_j=Σq_ijF_ij+(ε_j+2^(−j))H+C_j
are decreasing actual AFS and converge to Σp_i log|f_i|+C. They dominate that sum since F_ij≥log|f_i| and F_ij≤D_iH. Monotonicity follows from ε_j−ε_(j+1)≥ΣD_i(q_i,j+1−q_ij) and F_i,j+1≤F_ij. At a zero with p_i>0, that term tends to −∞ while all other terms are bounded above at the fixed point. Zero coefficients are omitted. The lower bounds F_ij≥2^(−j)H−j ensure that L_j dominates a positive multiple of H minus a finite constant, so original generator branches may be appended at sufficiently low rational weights without changing the function. Positive rational sums distribute into finite logarithmic monomial maxima. No uniform approximation at logarithmic poles is assumed.

For normal divisor-order localization, let A be a normal integral affine algebra over the original k, f≠0, h∈A_f, and U an actual global rational AFS. Suppose b+a log|h|≤max(U,−c log|f|)+C on Spec(A_f)^an, with a,c>0. On rays r ord_D at any prime divisor D, U is bounded above because its branches are regular. Sending r→∞ gives a max(−ord_D h,0)≤c ord_D f. These are orders of the actual rational functions. For f=z²,h=z^(−1),a=2,c=1 this is equality; a chosen denominator exponent would give a misleading budget.

For positive integers r,q with q/r>c/a, h^r f^q has no prime-divisor poles and belongs to A by the accepted normal height-one DVR intersection property. Thus no normalization hull replaces the original ring's hull. If x is in the A-polynomial hull of compact L⊂Spec(A_f)^an and |log|f||≤M on L∪{x}, the hull inequality for h^rf^q gives a log|h(x)|+b≤sup_L(a log|h|+b)+2a(q/r)M. Let q/r↓c/a to obtain the bound with 2cM. If h(x)=0 it is immediate; if h vanishes throughout L, the same polynomial forces h(x)=0. Controlled approximation of a weak input on A_f is still a separate missing antecedent before a Runge application.

For the carrier issue, let q:Y→Y be a continuous retraction on compact Hausdorff Y, image B, and U=U∘q bounded above. Then U_Y*|B=(U|B)_B*. A neighborhood N of b in B has q^(−1)(N) as an ambient neighborhood, and the two suprema of U agree. This gives one limsup inequality; restricting ambient neighborhoods gives the other. No openness is required. At a rational quotient, the accepted residual torification identifies B with K through the calibrated Gauss lift. Splitting projective FS sections into residual weight components with their original coefficients constructs actual globally generating ψ∘q≥ψ; uniform and decreasing limits preserve membership. Thus an independently proved unrestricted projective EP would imply carrier usc-sup membership by torifying its actual envelope and using this retraction identity. It is not an unconditional EP proof.

Raw-root usc transport is independently checked on Ω≅K×R. For a uniformly upper-bounded family U=sup_i u_i, the accepted orbit inequalities with uniform 0<c≤C also hold for U*. Roots satisfy R(sup_i u_i)=sup_i Ru_i: above the supremal root all branches are uniformly negative, and below it one is positive. They also satisfy R(U*)=(RU)*. Above the root, usc gives a negative neighborhood which the fixed inverse action pulls back to an upper root bound; below it, every neighborhood meets {U>0}, giving the lower root-limsup bound. The −∞ case uses the upper argument for every parameter. Applying the accepted actual raw inverse transports carrier envelope membership between Reeb fields only after a base exists. It does not transport I completeness or strong topology.

The source E is exactly 2609.27610v1, PDF SHA256 11808a6c9ede9c0158b27e16700fc180a4ac8df12a4586a7178e1958e8f6bba8, extract SHA256 c8ffe91a631da67f6d3872a1a06ab8d15755aed2f926cdf326725ca3662cef7d. Inclusive one-based LF coordinates use UTF-8 decode and split('\n'). Definition 3.15 at LF766–768 prints LOWER growth. Proposition 4.19 at LF1560–1562 asserts equality with decreasing global AFS regularizability; its proof LF1569–1572 seeks an upper bound and invokes Lemma 3.25(1), whose LF952–957 antecedent already includes regularizability.

The printed lower-growth proposition is false. On A1, v=(max(log|z|,0))² is locally psh by decreasing rational dyadic secants of t² on [−M,0], extended by zero for t≥0, where t=−log|z| and M>0 is rational. Near t=∞ the approximants are constant zero, meeting the finite active-affine chart condition. The global AFS g=max(log|z|,0) satisfies g≤v+1/4. On the Gauss ray |z|=e^t, every global AFS is bounded by At+B because each polynomial has log norm (deg f)t. No first decreasing approximant can dominate t² for all t≥0. This refutes the printed formulation, not a corrected upper-growth EP theorem.

Indispensable unreconstructed steps remain: actual strict Laurent/formal metric representation and analytic curve unit balancing; represented nef metrics and same-class BE/Gauss descent; common collars, weighted local products, smooth-target removal and determinant/radial traces; a weak split-piece argument on one proper witness with whole winning collars, a compatible locally constant integer trace, and γ=1 separately; weak Hartogs Runge before coefficient radii; finite projection and reduced singular-stratum induction; countable rational normal EP; and finite PL/reference descent with exact positive MA base change, orthogonality and domination. E Theorem 7.1 LF2704–2717 explicitly invokes weak/global Theorem 6.5 and does not bypass that chain. Continuous integer traces need not be constant on a disconnected open. None of these source conclusions is silently assumed.

notes.text:
The unchanged original P13.2 is not solved. Notes n1–n3 retain the original normal-cone domain, arbitrary algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, every rational and irrational Reeb field, fixed carrier K=X0^T and genuine affine-cone probability normalization. They establish reconstructed finite-target and approximation results, a new fixed-ray polynomial Hölder application and uniform signed target-integration estimate, and elementary normal-envelope auxiliaries. No all-dimensional intrinsic image sufficiency or actual inverse existence is claimed.

The indispensable gap is actual realization: prove actual E1 membership of the I-Cauchy maximizing limits, or complete the normal rational envelope base and then establish genuine normalized PSH compactness, weak bounded-J target L1 continuity, energy usc and variational attainment at each fixed irrational field. The signed estimates and convergence of output dual energies do not imply these missing claims. The synthetic finite polynomial theorem has been justified; the full ordered-linear/model/ample/generated-PSH topology and actual inverse application have not. Roots transfer carrier envelope membership only after a rational base exists and do not transport a strong topology. A weak limit of genuine MA measures is not labeled an output without its actual potential. Dimension one is solved separately and does not replace the original problem.
